headline: Low pairwise risk overall: no shared channels or write surfaces are documented, so prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors are largely blocked by the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langchain4j has no documented shared channel to pathway, and pathway exposes no clipboard, stdin/stdout, MCP, or filesystem bridge. With both profiles showing no direct ingestion path, a prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies langchain4j output into pathway inputs, then injection becomes possible.
IF either agent is connected through a shared file or message queue not listed in the profiles, reassess.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected except through explicit, typed APIs.
Disable any ad hoc copy-paste bridge between outputs and inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither agent is documented to read or write files, use clipboard, or egress network traffic. Langchain4j and pathway also touch no data classes here, so there is no documented path for sensitive data to flow between them.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to read shared files, leakage risk increases.
IF a third-party backend is introduced for either agent, reassess data exposure.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared workspace.
Review future connector settings before enabling them.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pathway cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, and langchain4j has no documented write or git capability in the profile. Without overlapping mutable surfaces, capability conflict is not plausible from the provided profiles.
conditions: IF langchain4j is wrapped with a separate writer or git client, conflict risk should be re-evaluated.
IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, conflict becomes possible.
mitigations: Do not add shared writable mounts.
requires-engineering: add lockfiles or transactional writes if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error pathway is not documented because pathway has no action-taking authority and no input/output bridge is shown. Langchain4j can still generate content that a downstream system might trust, but the pair itself lacks evidence of automatic execution or verification bypass.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds langchain4j output directly into pathway without validation, cascading error risk increases.
IF pathway is later configured to trigger downstream actions from model text, reassess.
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step between agents.
Require schema validation on all langchain4j outputs.
Log and review any downstream actions triggered by generated text.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either langchain4j or pathway, so no compliance mismatch is evidenced. Because the profiles are silent, the other agent is not cited beyond the absence of relevant compliance fields.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced, compliance must be rechecked.
IF either vendor publishes differing retention or residency terms, reassess.
mitigations: requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
